newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin recovering, soon back at helm -Russian PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin recovering, soon back at helm -Russian PM.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is recovering well from open heart surgery and will soon resume full command of affairs, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday

Speaking after his first full working meeting with Yeltsin since the president underwent quintuple bypass surgery on November 5, Chernomyrdin told reporters: "He is recovering. All is going as it should."

"Soon we shall all feel that the president is in place, at work. I am very glad about this," said Chernomyrdin, who assumed many of Yeltsin's responsibilities during his illness and had met him briefly and informally shortly after the operation.
Chernomyrdin met Yeltsin at the Central Clinical Centre just outside Moscow where he is convalescing.
The prime minister said their talks had been very "businesslike," adding that the president was taking an active interest in all matters.
"Above all he is interested in the question of wage payments and the state of the whole social sphere," he said.

Non-payment of wages has become an acute social problem affecting millions of people, including army officers, teachers and doctors across the sprawling Russian Federation. The government blames tax dodgers for the delays.
Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters on Tuesday that Yeltsin, gradually building up his daily workload, would probably move to the Barvikha sanatorium later this week.
Yeltsin's nearly four-month absence from the Kremlin because of his illness has been marked by a worsening economic crisis and infighting between members of his entourage jostling for influence.
